verdict: [V] At multiplicative_depth=50 the same two-block context (batch_slots=4096, 63 rotation keys, dnum=2 HYBRID key switching) reaches much further into FIDESlib's LoadContext than at depth=64 -- it prints its own bootstrap-precomputation-loading progress lines and then fails with an explicit, cleanly-checked CUDA allocation error at ~81GB used (of 81920 MiB total), rather than the unexplained SIGSEGV seen at depth=64 (fhe_fides_gpu_multiblock_blocks0_1_refresh_FAIL_20260724.json). This supersedes that record's diagnosis, which had ruled out GPU memory exhaustion based on a peak-usage measurement of only ~2GB during the depth=64 run: that measurement was real but misleading, because the depth=64 run crashes so much earlier (before any of LoadContext's own progress output) that it never reaches the large allocations at all. The corrected diagnosis: this two-block context's GPU memory footprint -- driven by batch_slots=4096 and 63 rotation keys under HYBRID key switching with dnum=2 -- does not fit in one A100's 80GB regardless of exact depth in the 50-64 range tested. Lowering multiplicative_depth alone is not a fix. [U] Reducing the memory footprint requires cutting batch_slots and/or the rotation-key count (e.g. a smaller BSGS rotation set), switching key-switching technique/digit count, or splitting the computation across multiple GPUs -- not yet attempted.
